central_model: Use a three-layer review knowledge model: a stable, identifier-based Foundation of entities and relations; purpose-specific Linearizations for screening, extraction, synthesis, and reporting; and constrained postcoordination for study-specific detail. This separates reusable meaning from workflow views while retaining links to the same underlying entities.

architecture_principles.principle: Represent each report, study, workflow, causal link, contrast, validation activity, and evidence item as a distinct typed entity with a persistent unique identifier and explicit properties/relationships.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Prevents a publication from being conflated with the study it describes, or a causal claim with the workflow and evidence supporting it; stable identifiers permit unambiguous cross-links.

architecture_principles.principle: Maintain a multidimensional Foundation that permits multiple parents and non-mutually-exclusive relationships; derive task-specific single-parent views from it.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: A study can support several pathways, omics layers, outcomes, and reports without forced duplication, while reviewers can still use simple, purpose-built extraction and synthesis views.

architecture_principles.principle: Separate the canonical content layer from operational rules and generated views.
architecture_principles.source_locator: §3.2 “WHO-FIC Model Architecture: Content Model, Foundation, and Linearizations,” Fig. 1; §4.12 “Linearization Specifications”
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Lets the review preserve one evidence base while producing different displays or exports for causal-link tables, validation summaries, and report-level bibliographies.

architecture_principles.principle: Model compound descriptions as a base entity plus constrained axes/value sets; pre-coordinate only combinations that deserve stable named entities.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Captures heterogeneous study features—e.g., omics layer, tissue, age window, exposure, outcome, adjustment set, estimand, and validation type—without creating a separate entity for every combination.

architecture_principles.principle: Declare which fields are allowed, required, repeatable, and value-constrained for each entity type or review view.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Makes causal-link records comparable and prevents invalid combinations, while allowing legitimately multi-valued features such as multiple omics assays or validation datasets.

architecture_principles.principle: Distinguish fully defining conditions from facts that are merely always true.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Avoids overstating causality: a causal link should receive a logical definition only when its full conditions are specified; otherwise record asserted necessary properties such as measured tissue, temporal ordering, or reported adjustment.

architecture_principles.principle: Use explicit inclusions, exclusions, synonyms, and boundary references around entities.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Supports search and harmonization without silently merging near-neighbor constructs, such as biological aging proxies, different causal estimands, or different validation standards.

architecture_principles.principle: Record lifecycle status and backwards-compatibility mappings.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Preserves auditability when terminology, measurement platforms, or review coding conventions change.

unit_and_boundary_rules: Report is a bibliographic/source entity; Study is the underlying empirical investigation. Link reports to the study or studies they describe rather than merging them.
Causal workflow is a distinct entity linked to its study, with ordered or typed steps; it is not identical to any resulting causal link.

Causal link is the claim-level entity linking exposure/intervention, molecular feature or mediator, outcome, population/context, and estimand. A contrast is a separate specification of the comparison that identifies the link.
Validation is a distinct activity/entity linked to the causal link or workflow, its target claim, dataset/cohort, and result; do not treat its presence as a property-only shortcut.
Source evidence is an atomic provenance entity—such as a quoted result, table, figure, supplement, or methods passage—linked to the report and to the exact extracted assertion.

Allow polyhierarchy in the Foundation (e.g., one molecular feature or workflow can participate in several causal links); generate mutually exclusive, single-parent views only when a particular review task requires them.
Use a canonical, unambiguous fully specified name for every controlled entity; retain aliases as synonyms and record exclusions for concepts that must remain separate.
provenance_and_evidence_rules: Every extracted field or relation should point to one or more source-evidence entities, and each evidence entity should identify its report and locator.
Keep Foundation-level assertions separate from generated review views, mirroring the guide’s separation between common content and linearization-specific operational knowledge.
Tag evidence with status appropriate to the review (e.g., extracted, adjudicated, superseded) rather than overwriting prior assertions; retain backward mappings when terms or coding change.

Represent uncertainty as structured detail or a constrained value, not as an implicit absence; use distinct residual/unspecified categories only when source documentation lacks the needed information.
Use formal necessary conditions for universally asserted characteristics of a record; reserve necessary-and-sufficient definitions for tightly specified, machine-checkable patterns.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Canonical graph of Report, Study, Cohort, Dataset, Workflow, CausalLink, Contrast, Validation, EvidenceItem, biomolecular entities, and controlled value sets.
Generate distinct views for screening, full-text extraction, causal-claim synthesis, evidence audit, and aging/omics specialty subsets, all pointing back to canonical entities.
Attach constrained axes for omics modality, feature type, tissue/cell type, time/age, exposure, outcome, causal method, covariate/assumption profile, effect direction, and validation design.
Create stable named workflow patterns only for recurrent combinations; encode the defining sequence and settings as a computable conjunction when warranted.
Use inclusions for exemplary compatible evidence, exclusions for explicitly non-equivalent claims, and ‘related elsewhere’ links for semantically close entities that appear in another synthesis view.

cautions: The guide is a classification-content architecture, not a causal-inference standard; it does not establish what constitutes valid causal identification or validation in multi-omics research.
Do not interpret an ‘associated with’ relation as causal: §4.13.1.15 explicitly says it does not specify the exact meaning of the relationship.
Do not make every observed feature a logical definition. The guide distinguishes necessary conditions from sufficient conditions (§3.9–3.10).
Linearizations must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive (§3.5), but the canonical Foundation need not be; do not impose a single-parent taxonomy on the underlying evidence graph.
The source describes operational and API possibilities that were draft/work-in-progress in places; adopt the architectural pattern, not its ICD-specific axes or implementation details verbatim.
